files.polish.md: arm B - the model's full polish of arm A, prompt prompt/polish.md
files.polish2.md: arm B second sample, same prompt, for the determinism measurement (6 episodes)
files.template.md: arm A - rendered by recommender.narrative.template, not by the model
files.why.md: arm C - the model's single why-sentence, prompt prompt/why.md

how: The model that ran this spike generated the arm B and arm C texts itself, in-session, from the pinned prompts in ../prompt/ and the recorded citation index in ../evidence/. There is no API key, provider SDK or outbound endpoint in the spike sandbox, so the arms are recorded artefacts on disk rather than live calls, and re-running the spike re-reads them instead of asking the model again - which is the property you want in a report a CI job can check.

model.harness: pi coding agent, reasoning level medium

what_that_costs: cost and latency for arms B and C are MODELLED from recorded character counts at a reference price band (spike.REFERENCE), not measured against a bill or a clock; the ship decision is gated on re-measuring them against a real provider endpoint
sampling parameters are the harness's, not chosen for this experiment, and cannot be re-set

one base model authored the narratives, the resamples and the three reviewer passes, so arm quality and panel ratings share a bias the panel cannot see; the mechanical audit in audit.py is the part of the measurement that does not depend on that model being any good

the author knew the audit's rules, because the same session wrote them - the strongest reason the zero hallucination count is read as an upper bound on a disciplined arm, not as a rate a stranger would hit
